title: Candy Corn Bag

drivers.name: Price increase (6.0%)
drivers.evidence: Last week at $4.08, sales were 3 units (vs baseline 10.3), a 71% drop. No promotion; price is higher than regular. Past promotions show uplift, but this is a price hike, not a discount.

drivers.name: Supplier delivery warning
drivers.evidence: Planner note indicates possible supply disruption. Not a full stoppage, but may suppress demand or cause stockouts. Adds downside risk. Not quantified directly but plausible.

adjustment.analysis: Baseline median is 10.3. Price increased 6.0% to $4.08, above regular $3.85. Past promotions show median uplift x2.15 vs baseline, but noise-adjusted x1.45. This price hike is not a promotion, so it likely reduces demand. The recent week (2026-10-05) at $4.08 sold only 3 units (vs baseline 10.3), a 71% drop—strong evidence of price sensitivity. Supplier delivery warning adds downside risk. No event or promotion. Classical model suggests no uplift, but that ignores price effect. Adjust down: noise-adjusted price effect from recent week is x0.29. Combine with supply risk (moderate confidence). Shrink toward 1.0 due to limited data. Final multiplier <1.0.

brief:
PRODUCT: Candy Corn Bag | category Candy | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-08 (4 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 4.08 (+6.0% vs regular price 3.85)
  planner notes: Supplier warns of a short delivery

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 10.3 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 24.6 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 19.2

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-85% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
